body.translated_text: The condensed meaning of the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom in Eight Thousand [Lines])

children.translated_text: In the ocean of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), a treasury of auspicious jewels itself,

children.text: sarvā pāramitās tatra tādātmyena vyavasthitāḥ // Nś_1 //
children.translated_text: all <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) are established therein in essential identity. // 1 //
Without elaboration, without appearance, without conceptual construction, without basis,
without inherent nature, supreme, subtle, devoid of <s>bindu</s> (point) and <s>nāda</s> (sound). // 2 //
<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the Mother, the source of all <s>Buddhas</s>, supreme,
of the nature of the threefold non-apprehension, the domain of the knowledge of the Omniscient. // 3 //
Whoever wishes to properly cultivate <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,
by that one, these nine verses should be contemplated in their meaning, in summary. // 4 //
Arisen from the power of <s>karma</s>, characterized by the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>),

children.text: punarbhavam iti khyātaṃ pratibhāsopamaṃ hi tat // Nś_5_[1] //
children.translated_text: known as 'rebirth' (<s>punarbhava</s>)—it is like a reflection. // 5 [1] //

body.text:
nirmitaṃ nagaraṃ yadvad vilokayati nirmitaḥ /
tadvat paśyati rūpāṇi karmabhir ni

children.translated_text: by

body.translated_text:
Just as a magically created being beholds a magically created city,
so does it behold forms—the world created

children.text: dharmaṃ deśayataḥ śabdā ye kecit śrutigocarāḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever sounds are within the range of hearing when the <s>Dharma</s> is being taught,
they are all like echoes—sounds arisen from hearing that have been heard. // 7 [3] //
What is smelled, tasted, and likewise touched by those attached to sense-objects—

children.text: svapnatulyam idaṃ sarvam upalabdhaṃ na vidyate // Nś_8_[4] //
children.translated_text: all this is like a dream; what is apprehended does not [truly] exist. // 8 [4] //

children.text: māyāyantro naro yadvad bhinnāṃ ceṣṭāṃ karoti vai /
children.translated_text: Just as a man [who is] a mechanical puppet performs various actions,

children.text: tadvad ceṣṭāṃ karoty eva dehayantro nirātmakaḥ // Nś_9_[5] //
children.translated_text: so too does the selfless body-puppet perform its actions. // 9 [5] //
The various apprehensions that arise moment by moment
are like mirages—seen then vanished, of diverse character. // 10 [6] //
The apprehended, resembling a reflection, arises from beginningless mind;
and consciousness, of that very form, is like a mutual reflection. // 11 [7] //
in [whose] pure mind-streams,
that which
arises like a moon from knowledge—

children.text: udakacandropamaṃ tad dhi pratyakṣaṃ na vidyate // Nś_12_[8] //
children.translated_text: like a moon [reflected] in water, that direct perception does not [truly] exist. // 12 [8] //

children.text: yoginām api yaj jñānaṃ tad apy ākāśalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Even the knowledge of <s>yogins</s>—that too has the nature of space;

children.text: tasmāj jñānaṃ ca jñeyaṃ ca sarvam ākāśalakṣaṇam // Nś_13_[9] //
children.translated_text: therefore, both knowledge and the knowable—everything has the nature of space. // 13 [9] //
Thus, for one who contemplates reality, unsupported in all phenomena,
through the mind of aspiration for awakening (<s>bodhipraṇidhicitta</s>), supreme knowledge shall arise. // 14 //

body.text:
āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ piṇḍārthaḥ samāptaḥ
kṛtir iyaṃ śrīkam

children.translated_text: b
<s>alāmbarapāda</s> (<s>Kambalapāda</s>).

body.translated_text:
The condensed meaning of the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> is completed.
This is the composition of the glorious <s>Kam</s>-
